claims.statement: Meretseger is a Theban cobra goddess protecting the necropolis and Valley of the Kings.
claims.statement_id: Meretseger adalah dewi kobra Thebes yang melindungi nekropolis dan Lembah Para Raja.
claims.quote: Meretseger (also known as Mersegrit' or Mertseger) was a Theban cobra-goddess in ancient Egyptian religion, in charge with guarding and protecting the vast Theban Necropolis — on the west bank of the Nile, in front of Thebes — and especially the heavily guarded Valley of the Kings. Her cult was typical of the New Kingdom of Egypt (1550–1070 BC).

claims.statement: Her name means She Who Loves Silence, with another interpretation connected with Osiris.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berarti Yang Mencintai Keheningan, dengan tafsir lain berkaitan dengan Osiris.
claims.quote: Meretseger's name means "She Who Loves Silence", in reference to the silence of the desert cemetery area she kept or, according to another interpretation, "Beloved of Him Who Makes Silence (Osiris)".

claims.statement: She is patron of Deir el-Medina’s artisans and workers.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjadi pelindung perajin dan pekerja Deir el-Medina.
claims.quote: Meretseger was the patron of the artisans and workers of the village of Deir el-Medina, who built and decorated the great royal and noble tombs.

claims.statement: Small rock temples are dedicated to Meretseger.
claims.statement_id: Kuil batu kecil didedikasikan kepada Meretseger.
claims.quote: only small rock temples were dedicated to her

claims.statement: She is believed to punish transgressions with a poisonous bite but heal the repentant.
claims.statement_id: Ia dipercaya menghukum pelanggaran dengan gigitan beracun tetapi menyembuhkan orang yang bertobat.
claims.quote: It was believed that Meretseger punished the workers who committed a sacrilege (by stealing something from the royal graves or the building sites — copper instruments were particularly precious — as well as those who failed in an oath) poisoning them with her bite.

claims.statement: The accompanying encyclopedia confirms her protection of the Valley of the Kings.
claims.statement_id: Ensiklopedia pendamping menegaskan perlindungannya atas Lembah Para Raja.
claims.quote: Meretseger - A protector goddess in the form of a cobra venerated at Thebes. Specifically, she guarded the necropolis of the Valley of the Kings.

claims.statement: Aker is an Egyptian earth and underworld god guarding the eastern and western horizons.
claims.statement_id: Aker adalah dewa bumi dan dunia bawah Mesir yang menjaga cakrawala timur dan barat.
claims.quote: Aker was an ancient Egyptian personification of the horizon, and an earth and underworld god, believed to guard the eastern (Bakhu) and western (Manu) horizons.

claims.statement: His early image is a recumbent lion torso with an open mouth.
claims.statement_id: Gambaran awalnya berupa tubuh singa berbaring dengan mulut terbuka.
claims.quote: Aker was first depicted as the torso of a recumbent lion with a widely opened mouth. Later, he was depicted as two recumbent lion torsos merged with each other and still looking away from each other.

claims.statement: His paired lions are named Duaj, tomorrow, and Sefe, yesterday.
claims.statement_id: Sepasang singanya bernama Duaj, esok, dan Sefe, kemarin.
claims.quote: From Middle Kingdom onwards Aker appears as a pair of twin lions, one named Duaj (meaning "tomorrow") and the other Sefe (meaning "yesterday"). Aker was thus often titled "He who's looking forward and behind". When depicted as a lion pair, a hieroglyphic sign for "horizon" (two merged mountains) and a sun disc was put between the lions; the lions were sitting back-on-back.

claims.statement: Another form joins two human-headed sphinx torsos.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk lain memadukan tubuh dua sfinks berkepala manusia.
claims.quote: In later times, Aker can also appear as two merged torsos of recumbent sphinxes with human heads.

claims.statement: He protects the deceased king from demonic serpents.
claims.statement_id: Ia melindungi raja wafat dari ular-ular setan.
claims.quote: Aker was first described as one of the earth gods guarding the "gate to the yonder site". He protected the deceased king against the three demonic snakes Hemtet, Iqeru and Jagw. By "encircling" (i.e. interring) the deceased king, Aker sealed the deceased away from the poisonous breath of the snake demons. Another earth deity, who joined and promoted Aker's work, was Geb.

claims.statement: Aker protects Ra’s barque as it enters and leaves the underworld.
claims.statement_id: Aker melindungi bahtera Ra saat memasuki dan meninggalkan dunia bawah.
claims.quote: He protected the sun barge of Ra as it entered and left the underworld at dusk and dawn.

claims.statement: Bennu is an Egyptian avian deity associated with the sun, creation and rebirth.
claims.statement_id: Bennu adalah dewa Mesir berbentuk burung yang berkaitan dengan matahari, penciptaan, dan kelahiran kembali.
claims.quote: is an ancient Egyptian deity linked with the Sun, creation, and rebirth.

claims.statement: He is said to create himself and be Ra’s ba.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikatakan menciptakan diri sendiri dan menjadi ba Ra.
claims.quote: According to Egyptian mythology, Bennu was a self-created being said to have played a role in the creation of the world. He was said to be the ba (personality component of the soul) of the sun deity Ra, and to have enabled the creative actions of Atum.

claims.statement: He flies over Nun’s waters and calls out to determine creation.
claims.statement_id: Ia terbang di atas air Nun dan berseru sehingga menentukan penciptaan.
claims.quote: The deity was said to have flown over the waters of Nun that existed before creation, landing on a rock and issuing a call that determined the nature of creation.

claims.statement: His name is linked with wbn, to rise in brilliance or shine.
claims.statement_id: Namanya dikaitkan dengan kata wbn, terbit bercahaya atau bersinar.
claims.quote: His name is related to the Egyptian verb wbn, meaning "to rise in brilliance" or "to shine".

claims.statement: New Kingdom art depicts him as a great grey heron.
claims.statement_id: Seni Kerajaan Baru menggambarkannya sebagai bangau abu-abu besar.
claims.quote: New Kingdom artwork shows Bennu as a huge grey heron with a long beak and a two-feathered crest. Sometimes Bennu is depicted as perched on a benben stone (representing Ra and the name of the top stone of a pyramid) or in a willow tree (representing Osiris). Because of the connection with Osiris, Bennu sometimes wears the Atef crown, instead of the solar disk.

claims.statement: The accompanying encyclopedia connects Bennu with the origin of Greek Phoenix legends.
claims.statement_id: Ensiklopedia pendamping mengaitkan Bennu dengan asal legenda Phoenix Yunani.
claims.quote: inspiration for the Greek Phoenix.

claims.statement: Satis is an Upper Egyptian goddess in the Elephantine triad with Khnum and Anuket.
claims.statement_id: Satis adalah dewi Mesir Hulu dalam triad Elephantine bersama Khnum dan Anuket.
claims.quote: was an Upper Egyptian goddess who, along with Khnum and Anuket, formed part of the Elephantine Triad.

claims.statement: She protects the Nubian border and personifies the Nile inundation.
claims.statement_id: Ia melindungi perbatasan Nubia dan mempersonifikasikan banjir Nil.
claims.quote: A protective deity of Egypt's southern border with Nubia, she came to personify the former annual flooding of the Nile

claims.statement: She is equated with Hera and Juno in Greek interpretation.
claims.statement_id: Ia disetarakan dengan Hera dan Juno dalam interpretasi Yunani.
claims.quote: She was sometimes conflated with Isis and Sopdet, goddess of the bright star Sirius, which the Egyptians connected with the onset of the Nile flooding. Under the interpretatio graeca, she was conflated with Hera and Juno.

claims.statement: Her name can mean She Who Shoots or She Who Pours.
claims.statement_id: Namanya dapat berarti Yang Menembak atau Yang Menuang.
claims.quote: her name can be variously translated as "She who Shoots" or "She who Pours" depending on which of her roles is being emphasized.

claims.statement: The Pyramid Texts describe her purifying a dead pharaoh’s body with Elephantine water.
claims.statement_id: Teks Piramida mengisahkannya memurnikan tubuh firaun wafat dengan air Elephantine.
claims.quote: A goddess of the Upper Egyptians, her cult is first attested on jars beneath the Step Pyramid of Saqqara (Dynasty III). She appears in the Pyramid Texts (Dynasty VI) purifying a deceased pharaoh's body with four jars of water from Elephantine.

claims.statement: Satis is shown wearing Upper Egypt’s White Crown with antelope horns.
claims.statement_id: Satis digambarkan memakai Mahkota Putih Mesir Hulu dengan tanduk antelop.
claims.quote: She is depicted as a woman wearing the White Crown of Upper Egypt with antelope horns.

claims.statement: Bat is an Egyptian cow goddess shown with a human face, cow ears and horns.
claims.statement_id: Bat adalah dewi sapi Mesir yang digambarkan dengan wajah manusia, telinga sapi, dan tanduk.
claims.quote: Bat is a cow goddess in Egyptian mythology who was depicted as a human face with cow ears and horns or as a woman. Evidence of the worship of Bat exists from the earliest records of the religious practices in ancient Egypt.

claims.statement: She is chief goddess of Seshesh or Hu in Upper Egypt’s seventh nome.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjadi dewi utama Seshesh atau Hu di nome ketujuh Mesir Hulu.
claims.quote: The worship of Bat dates to earliest times in ancient Egypt and may have its origins in Late Paleolithic cattle herding cultures. Bat was the chief goddess of Seshesh, otherwise known as Hu or Diospolis Parva, the 7th nome of Upper Egypt.

claims.statement: Her name may be related to ba with the feminine ending t.
claims.statement_id: Namanya mungkin terkait ba dengan akhiran feminin t.
claims.quote: The epithet, Bat, may be linked to the word ba with the feminine suffix 't'. A person's ba roughly equates to one's personality or emanation and often is translated as 'soul'.

claims.statement: Bat is associated with the sistrum and her cult centre is called Mansion of the Sistrum.
claims.statement_id: Bat terkait sistrum dan pusat kultusnya disebut Rumah Sistrum.
claims.quote: Bat became strongly associated with the sistrum and the center of her cult was known as the "Mansion of the Sistrum". The sistrum is an ankh-shaped musical instrument, which was one of the most frequently used sacred instruments in ancient Egyptian temples.

claims.statement: Bat’s horns curve inward, unlike Hathor’s horns.
claims.statement_id: Tanduk Bat melengkung ke dalam, berbeda dari tanduk Hathor.
claims.quote: The imagery of Bat as a divine cow was remarkably similar to that of Hathor, a parallel goddess from another nome. In two dimensional images, both goddesses often are depicted straight on, facing the onlooker and not in profile in accordance with the characteristic Egyptian convention.

claims.statement: Bat is believed to see past and future and thereby grant success.
claims.statement_id: Bat dipercaya melihat masa lalu dan masa depan, sehingga memberi keberhasilan.
claims.quote: She blessed people with success owing to her ability to see both past and future.

claims.statement: Harpocrates is a god of silence and secrecy in the Hellenistic religion developed at Alexandria.
claims.statement_id: Harpocrates adalah dewa keheningan dan kerahasiaan dalam agama Helenistik yang berkembang di Alexandria.
claims.quote: is the god of silence, secrets, and confidentiality, and a protector of reputations in the Hellenistic religion developed in Ptolemaic Alexandria

claims.statement: The Greeks adapt him from Horus the Child, representing the newborn sun.
claims.statement_id: Orang Yunani mengadaptasinya dari Horus Anak yang melambangkan matahari baru lahir.
claims.quote: Greeks adapted Harpocrates from the Egyptian child-god Horus, who represented the newborn sun, rising each day at dawn.

claims.statement: His name is a Greek form of Horus the Child.
claims.statement_id: Namanya merupakan bentuk Yunani dari Horus Sang Anak.
claims.quote: The name "Harpocrates" originated as a Hellenization of the Egyptian Har-pa-khered or Heru-pa-khered, meaning "Horus the Child".

claims.statement: A child’s finger-to-mouth gesture is interpreted by Greeks and Romans as silence.
claims.statement_id: Gerakan jari anak ke mulut ditafsirkan orang Yunani dan Romawi sebagai keheningan.
claims.quote: Horus the Child was portrayed as a naked boy with his finger to his mouth as if sucking on it, an Egyptian artistic convention for representing a child. Greeks and Romans misunderstood this pose as a gesture of silence and interpreted Harpocrates as the god of secrecy.

claims.statement: Horus-on-the-crocodiles stelae are used in water rites for blessing and healing.
claims.statement_id: Stela Horus di atas buaya digunakan dalam ritual air untuk berkat dan penyembuhan.
claims.quote: "Horus on the Crocodiles" steles depicting Heru-pa-Khered standing on the back of a crocodile and holding snakes in his outstretched hands were erected in Egyptian temple courtyards, where they would be immersed or lustrated (purified) in water; the water was then used for blessing and healing purposes as the name of Heru-pa-Khered was itself attributed with many protective and healing p

claims.statement: The accompanying source also depicts Harpocrates as a winged boy with a finger to his lips.
claims.statement_id: Sumber pendamping juga menggambarkan Harpocrates sebagai anak bersayap dengan jari pada bibir.
claims.quote: Harpocrates - The Greek and Roman name for Horus the Child, son of Osiris and Isis. Depicted as a young winged boy with his finger to his lips. He was venerated in Greece as the god of secrets, silence, and confidentiality.

claims.statement: Kek personifies primordial darkness in Egypt’s Hermopolitan Ogdoad.
claims.statement_id: Kek adalah personifikasi kegelapan primordial dalam Ogdoad Hermopolis di Mesir.
claims.quote: Kek is the deification of the concept of primordial darkness in the ancient Egyptian Ogdoad cosmogony of Hermopolis.

claims.statement: Kauket is his feminine counterpart or consort.
claims.statement_id: Kauket adalah aspek atau pasangan femininnya.
claims.quote: The Ogdoad consisted of four pairs of deities, four male gods paired with their female counterparts. Kek's female counterpart was Kauket. Kek and Kauket in some aspects also represent night and day, and were called "raiser up of the light" and the "raiser up of the night", respectively.

claims.statement: His written name is connected with the Egyptian word for darkness.
claims.statement_id: Ejaan namanya terkait kata Mesir untuk kegelapan.
claims.quote: The name is written as kk or kkwy with a variant of the sky hieroglyph in ligature with the staff (N2) associated with the word for "darkness" kkw.

claims.statement: Early images show Kek with a frog or cat head.
claims.statement_id: Gambar awal memperlihatkan Kek berkepala katak atau kucing.
claims.quote: In the oldest representations, Kauket is given the head of a serpent, and Kek the head of either a frog or a cat. In one scene, they are identified with Ka and Kait; in this scene, Ka-Kekui has the head of a frog surmounted by a beetle and Kait-Kekuit has the head of a serpent surmounted by a disk.

claims.statement: In the Greco-Roman period he is shown as a frog-headed man.
claims.statement_id: Pada masa Yunani-Romawi ia digambarkan sebagai laki-laki berkepala katak.
claims.quote: In the Greco-Roman period, Kek's male form was depicted as a frog-headed man, and the female form as a serpent-headed woman, as were all four dualistic concepts in the Ogdoad.

claims.statement: Kek and Kauket’s darkness is not understood as evil in this source.
claims.statement_id: Kegelapan Kek dan Kauket tidak dipahami sebagai kejahatan dalam sumber ini.
claims.quote: Kek and Kauket were the male/female aspects of darkness but not in any way associated with evil.

claims.statement: Maahes is a lion-headed war god in Egyptian religion.
claims.statement_id: Maahes adalah dewa perang berkepala singa dalam agama Mesir.
claims.quote: was an ancient Egyptian lion-headed god of war

claims.statement: His titles include Lord of Slaughter and Wielder of the Knife.
claims.statement_id: Gelarnya mencakup Penguasa Pembantaian dan Pemegang Pisau.
claims.quote: The name of Maahes begins with the hieroglyphs for the male lion, although in isolation it also means (one who can) see in front. Some of the titles of Maahes were Lord of Slaughter, Wielder of the Knife, and The Scarlet Lord.

claims.statement: The earliest reference cited by the article dates to the New Kingdom.
claims.statement_id: Rujukan tertua yang dicatat artikel berasal dari Kerajaan Baru.
claims.quote: The first recorded reference to Maahes is from the New Kingdom. Some Egyptologists have suggested that Maahes was of foreign origin; indeed there is some evidence that he may have been identical with the lion-god Apedemak worshipped in Nubia and Egypt's Western Desert.

claims.statement: He is regarded as a son of Ra with Bastet or Sekhmet.
claims.statement_id: Ia dianggap putra Ra dengan Bastet atau Sekhmet.
claims.quote: Maahes was considered the son of Ra with the feline goddess Bastet, or of another feline goddess, Sekhmet. He was sometimes identified with another son of Sekhmet, Nefertum. Maahes was said to fight Ra's archenemy, the serpent Apep, during Ra's nightly voyage.

claims.statement: He is shown holding a knife and lotus flowers.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan memegang pisau dan bunga teratai.
claims.quote: Maahes was pictured as a man with the head of a male lion, sometimes holding a knife and a bouquet of lotus flowers, referring to his connection with Nefertum, who was symbolized by the lotus.

claims.statement: The Greeks associate Maahes with the Furies because of his vengeful nature.
claims.statement_id: Orang Yunani menghubungkan Maahes dengan Furies karena watak pembalasannya.
claims.quote: Linked by the Greeks with the Furies because of his vengeful nature.

claims.statement: Onuris or Anhur is an Egyptian war god worshipped at Abydos and Thinis.
claims.statement_id: Onuris atau Anhur adalah dewa perang Mesir yang dipuja di Abydos dan Thinis.
claims.quote: was a war god who was worshipped in the Egyptian area of Abydos, and particularly in Thinis.

claims.statement: One myth tells of him bringing his consort Mehit from Nubia.
claims.statement_id: Satu mitos mengisahkan ia membawa pasangannya Mehit dari Nubia.
claims.quote: Myths told that he had brought his wife, Mehit, who was his female counterpart, from Nubia

claims.statement: He is shown bearded, wearing four feathers and carrying a spear.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan berjanggut, bermakhota empat bulu, dan membawa tombak.
claims.quote: One of his titles was slayer of enemies. Onuris was depicted as a bearded man wearing a robe and a headdress with four feathers, holding a spear or lance, or occasionally as a lion-headed god (representing strength and power). In some depictions, the robe was more similar to a kilt.

claims.statement: Mock battles are staged at festivals honouring him.
claims.statement_id: Pertempuran tiruan dilakukan dalam festival untuk menghormatinya.
claims.quote: at festivals honoring him, mock battles were staged.

claims.statement: The Greeks equate Onuris with Ares.
claims.statement_id: Orang Yunani menyetarakan Onuris dengan Ares.
claims.quote: The Greeks equated Onuris to their god of war, Ares. In the legend of Olympian gods fleeing from Typhon and taking animal form in Egypt, Ares was said to have taken the form of a fish as Lepidotus or Onuris.

claims.statement: Egyptian military banners show Anhur as protector of the troops.
claims.statement_id: Panji tentara Mesir menampilkan gambar Anhur sebagai pelindung pasukan.
claims.quote: His image (as Anhur) appeared on the banners of the Egyptian army

claims.statement: Heh personifies infinity or eternity in the Egyptian Ogdoad.
claims.statement_id: Heh adalah personifikasi ketakterhinggaan atau keabadian dalam Ogdoad Mesir.
claims.quote: Hẹh (hẹh, also Huh, Hah, Hauh, Huah, and Hehu) was the personification of infinity or eternity in the Ogdoad in ancient Egyptian religion. His name originally meant "flood", referring to the watery chaos Nu that the Egyptians believed existed before the creation of the world.

claims.statement: Hauhet is his feminine counterpart.
claims.statement_id: Hauhet adalah pasangan femininnya.
claims.quote: Heh's female counterpart and consort was known as Hauhet, which is simply the feminine form of his name.

claims.statement: He is often frog-headed and holds palm stems as symbols of long life.
claims.statement_id: Ia sering berkepala katak dan memegang batang palem sebagai lambang umur panjang.
claims.quote: Like the other concepts in the Ogdoad, his male form was often depicted as a frog, or a frog-headed human, and his female form as a snake or snake-headed human. The frog head symbolised fertility, creation, and regeneration, and was also possessed by the other Ogdoad males Kek, Amun, and Nun.

claims.statement: The accompanying source depicts Heh as a frog and Hauhet as a serpent.
claims.statement_id: Sumber pendamping menggambarkan Heh sebagai katak dan Hauhet sebagai ular.
claims.quote: Heh and Hauhet - God and goddess of infinity and eternity. Heh was depicted as a frog and Hauhet as a serpent.

claims.statement: In the Book of the Heavenly Cow, eight Heh beings support Nut with Shu.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Kitab Sapi Langit, delapan Heh bersama Shu menopang Nut.
claims.quote: Heh sometimes helps Shu, a god associated with air, in supporting the sky goddess Nut. In the Book of the Heavenly Cow, eight Heh gods are depicted together with Shu supporting Nut, who has taken the form of a cow.

claims.statement: The accompanying source identifies Heh and Hauhet as gods of infinity and eternity.
claims.statement_id: Sumber pendamping menempatkan Heh dan Hauhet sebagai dewa ketakterhinggaan dan keabadian.
claims.quote: Heh and Hauhet - God and goddess of infinity and eternity. Heh was depicted as a frog and Hauhet as a serpent. Their names mean "endlessness" and they were among the original gods of the Ogdoad.

claims.statement: Meskhenet is an Egyptian childbirth goddess creating each child’s ka.
claims.statement_id: Meskhenet adalah dewi kelahiran Mesir yang menciptakan ka setiap anak.
claims.quote: In ancient Egyptian mythology, Meskhenet, (also spelt  Mesenet, Meskhent, and Meshkent) was the goddess of childbirth, and the creator of each child's Ka, a part of their soul, which she breathed into them at the moment of birth. She was worshipped from the earliest of times by Egyptians.

claims.statement: She is associated with birth bricks and may be shown as a woman-headed brick.
claims.statement_id: Ia terkait bata kelahiran dan dapat digambarkan sebagai bata berkepala perempuan.
claims.quote: In ancient Egypt, women delivered babies while squatting on a pair of bricks, known as "birth bricks", and Meskhenet was the goddess associated with this form of delivery. Consequently, in art, she was sometimes depicted as a brick with a woman's head, wearing a cow's uterus upon it. At other times she was depicted as a woman with a symbolic cow's uterus on her headdress.

claims.statement: She is connected with fate and sometimes paired with Shai.
claims.statement_id: Ia berhubungan dengan nasib dan kadang dipasangkan dengan Shai.
claims.quote: Since she was responsible for creating the Ka, she was associated with fate. Thus later she was sometimes said to be paired with Shai, who became a god of destiny after the deity evolved out of an abstract concept.

claims.statement: The Westcar Papyrus tells of her presence at three future kings’ births.
claims.statement_id: Papirus Westcar mengisahkan kehadirannya saat tiga calon raja lahir.
claims.quote: Meskhenet features prominently in the last of the folktales in the Westcar Papyrus. The story tells of the birth of Userkaf, Sahure, and Neferirkare Kakai, the first three kings of the Fifth Dynasty, who in the story are said to be triplets. Just after each child is born, Meskhenet appears and prophesies that he will become king of Egypt.

claims.statement: She foretells that each infant will become king of Egypt.
claims.statement_id: Ia meramalkan setiap bayi tersebut akan menjadi raja Mesir.
claims.quote: Just after each child is born, Meskhenet appears and prophesies that he will become king of Egypt.

claims.statement: Meskhenet also comforts the soul during afterlife judgment.
claims.statement_id: Meskhenet juga menghibur jiwa pada pengadilan akhirat.
claims.quote: She was also present at the judgment of the soul in the afterlife as a comforter

claims.statement: The uraeus is an upright cobra representation in Egyptian tradition symbolizing royal power and divine authority.
claims.statement_id: Uraeus adalah gambaran kobra tegak dalam tradisi Mesir yang melambangkan kekuasaan kerajaan dan otoritas ilahi.
claims.quote: is the stylized, upright form of an Egyptian cobra, used as a symbol of sovereignty, royalty, deity and divine authority in ancient Egypt.

claims.statement: The uraeus represents the goddess Wadjet.
claims.statement_id: Uraeus merupakan lambang dewi Wadjet.
claims.quote: The uraeus is a symbol for the goddess Wadjet.

claims.statement: Its use on the crown signifies Wadjet’s protection of the pharaoh.
claims.statement_id: Pemakaiannya pada mahkota menandakan perlindungan Wadjet terhadap firaun.
claims.quote: this indicated Wadjet's protection and reinforced the pharaoh's claim over the land.

claims.statement: Nekhbet and Wadjet become the Two Ladies protecting unified Egypt.
claims.statement_id: Nekhbet dan Wadjet menjadi Dua Nyonya yang menjaga Mesir bersatu.
claims.quote: Together, they were known as the Nebty or the Two Ladies, who became the joint protectors and patrons of the unified Egypt.

claims.statement: Wadjet, represented by the uraeus, is described as Ra’s daughter and a figure in Eye of Ra stories.
claims.statement_id: Wadjet, yang dilambangkan uraeus, disebut putri Ra dan tokoh kisah Mata Ra.
claims.quote: She was the daughter of Ra and one of the goddesses featured in stories about the Eye of Ra.

claims.statement: The accompanying encyclopedia calls the uraeus the king’s insignia in the form of Wadjet’s rearing cobra.
claims.statement_id: Ensiklopedia pendamping menyebut uraeus sebagai insignia raja berupa kobra Wadjet yang terangkat.
claims.quote: represented as the rearing cobra which became the king's insignia (the uraeus).

claims.statement: Sopdu is an Egyptian god of the sky and eastern border regions.
claims.statement_id: Sopdu adalah dewa langit dan kawasan perbatasan timur Mesir.
claims.quote:
Sopdu (also rendered Septu or Sopedu) was a god of the sky and of eastern border regions in the religion of Ancient Egypt.
He was Khensit's husband.

claims.statement: Horus-Sopdu is called the offspring of Osiris-Sah and Isis-Sopdet in the Pyramid Texts.
claims.statement_id: Horus-Sopdu disebut anak Osiris-Sah dan Isis-Sopdet dalam Teks Piramida.
claims.quote: As a sky god, Sopdu was connected with the god Sah, the personification of the constellation Orion, and the goddess Sopdet, representing the star Sirius. According to the Pyramid Texts, Horus-Sopdu, a combination of Sopdu and the greater sky god Horus, is the offspring of Osiris-Sah and Isis-Sopdet.

claims.statement: He protects frontier outposts and helps the pharaoh control the eastern regions.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjaga pos-pos perbatasan dan membantu firaun mengendalikan kawasan timur.
claims.quote: As a god of the east, Sopdu was said to protect Egyptian outposts along the frontiers and to help the pharaoh control those regions' foreign inhabitants. He was referred to as Lord of the East, and had his greatest cult centre at the easternmost nome of Lower Egypt, which was named Per-Sopdu, meaning place of Sopdu.

claims.statement: His name is translated as sharp ones and connected with protecting the dead king’s teeth.
claims.statement_id: Namanya diterjemahkan sebagai yang tajam dan dihubungkan dengan perlindungan gigi raja wafat.
claims.quote: Sopdu's name is composed of the hieroglyph for sharp, a pointed triangle, and the 3rd person plural suffix (a quail); thus a literal translation of his name is sharp ones. He was said, in the Pyramid Texts, to protect the teeth of the deceased pharaoh.

claims.statement: He is depicted as a falcon or a warrior with an axe or spear.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai elang atau prajurit dengan kapak atau tombak.
claims.quote: Sopdu was depicted as a falcon sitting on a religious standard, often with a two-feathered crown on his head and a flail over his shoulder. In his border-guarding role he was shown as a Near Eastern warrior, with a shemset girdle and an axe or spear.

claims.statement: He helps ensure supplies reach eastern garrisons.
claims.statement_id: Ia membantu memastikan persediaan sampai ke garnisun timur.
claims.quote: he ensured the proper resources reached the eastern border garrisons

claims.statement: Heka is the deification of magic and medicine in ancient Egypt.
claims.statement_id: Heka adalah pendewaan sihir dan pengobatan dalam Mesir kuno.
claims.quote: was the deification of magic and medicine in ancient Egypt.

claims.statement: His name is identical to the Egyptian word for magic.
claims.statement_id: Namanya sama dengan kata Mesir untuk sihir.
claims.quote: The name Heka is identical with the Egyptian word ḥkꜣ(w) "magic". This hieroglyphic spelling includes the symbol for the word ka (kꜣ), the ancient Egyptian concept of the vital force. Due to the importance placed onto names in ancient Egypt Heka was often incorporated into personal names. Some examples include: Hekawy, Hekaf, or simply Heka.

claims.statement: The Pyramid Texts describe Heka as supernatural energy possessed by the gods.
claims.statement_id: Teks Piramida menggambarkan Heka sebagai energi supranatural para dewa.
claims.quote: The Old Kingdom Pyramid Texts depict Heka as a supernatural energy that the gods possess. The "cannibal pharaoh" must devour other gods to gain this magical power. Eventually, Heka was elevated to a deity in his own right, and a cult devoted to him developed.

claims.statement: Life and the world’s creation are connected with Heka’s power.
claims.statement_id: Kehidupan dan penciptaan dunia dikaitkan dengan kekuatan Heka.
claims.quote: Heka is said to have been created at the beginning of time by the creator Atum. According to the Egyptian cosmological belief their world was created through Heka. Heka was the primary force of life as a creative act according to the Egyptologist Ritner. Spell 648 of the Coffin Texts read:

claims.statement: He also appears as an Osiris protector in the Duat able to blind crocodiles.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga muncul sebagai pelindung Osiris di Duat yang dapat membutakan buaya.
claims.quote: Heka is later depicted as part of the tableau of the divine solar barque and as a protector of Osiris in Duat capable of blinding crocodiles.

claims.statement: Heka is patron of physicians and described as a primordial source of power.
claims.statement_id: Heka menjadi pelindung dokter dan disebut sebagai sumber daya primordial.
claims.quote: the patron god of magic and medicine but was also the primordial source of power in the universe.

claims.statement: Renenutet is an Egyptian goddess of grain, grapes, nourishment and harvest.
claims.statement_id: Renenutet adalah dewi Mesir untuk biji-bijian, anggur, nutrisi, dan panen.
claims.quote: was a goddess of grain, grapes, nourishment and the harvest in the ancient Egyptian religion.

claims.statement: She is shown as a cobra or cobra-headed woman.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai kobra atau perempuan berkepala kobra.
claims.quote: Renenutet was depicted as a cobra or as a woman with the head of a cobra.

claims.statement: She cares for the pharaoh from birth to death.
claims.statement_id: Ia merawat firaun sejak lahir hingga wafat.
claims.quote: The verbs "to fondle, to nurse, or rear" help explain the name Renenutet. This goddess was a "nurse" who took care of the pharaoh from birth to death. She was also called "the mistress of provisions", "Renenutet mistress of the offerings", "Renenutet mistress of the food", and "Renenutet the venerable of the double granary", and "who maintains everybody".

claims.statement: She is Shai’s feminine counterpart and protector of royal power.
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah pasangan feminin Shai dan pelindung kewenangan kerajaan.
claims.quote: She was the female counterpart of Shai, "destiny", who represented the positive destiny of the child. Renenutet was called Thermouthis or Hermouthis in Greek. She embodied the fertility of the fields (both the vegetation and the soil itself) and was the protector of the royal office and power.

claims.statement: Her images occur in kitchens and stores to protect food supplies.
claims.statement_id: Gambarnya berada di dapur dan tempat penyimpanan untuk menjaga persediaan makanan.
claims.quote: Offerings to Renenutet were depicted in Egyptian wine making scenes, and shrines to her were set up in vineyards. Images of her were found in kitchens, near ovens, in granaries, and in cellars. These images often invoked her to protect food stores against insects, mice, and snakes, not just as a provider of food. Her image also appears on stamps and stoppers for wine containers.

claims.statement: In the afterlife she bears the title Lady of Justification linking her with Maat.
claims.statement_id: Dalam akhirat ia memiliki gelar Nyonya Pembenaran yang menghubungkannya dengan Maat.
claims.quote: In the afterlife she appeared as the "Lady of Justification" linking her with the goddess Ma'at.

claims.statement: The serpopard is a mythical animal known from ancient Egyptian and Mesopotamian art.
claims.statement_id: Serpopard adalah hewan mitos yang dikenal dari seni Mesir kuno dan Mesopotamia.
claims.quote: is a mythical animal known from ancient Egyptian and Mesopotamian art.

claims.statement: Serpopard is a modern name blending serpent and leopard.
claims.statement_id: Nama serpopard adalah istilah modern gabungan serpent dan leopard.
claims.quote: The word "serpopard" is a modern coinage. It is a portmanteau of "serpent" and "leopard"

claims.statement: Its image appears on the Narmer and Oxford palettes.
claims.statement_id: Gambarnya muncul pada palet Narmer dan Oxford.
claims.quote: Examples include the Narmer Palette and the Oxford Palette.

claims.statement: Two beings are usually shown with intertwined necks.
claims.statement_id: Dua makhluk biasanya digambarkan dengan leher saling melilit.
claims.quote: Typically, two creatures are depicted, with their necks intertwined.

claims.statement: The depiction is also interpreted as an unusually long-necked lioness.
claims.statement_id: Penggambaran itu juga ditafsirkan sebagai singa betina berleher sangat panjang.
claims.quote: The image generally is classified as a feline, and with close  inspection resembles an unusually long-necked lioness.

claims.statement: One interpretation reads the being as chaos outside Egypt subdued by the king.
claims.statement_id: Satu penafsiran membaca makhluk itu sebagai kekacauan di luar Mesir yang ditundukkan raja.
claims.quote: It has been suggested that in Ancient Egyptian art the serpopard represents "a symbol of the chaos that reigned beyond Egypt's borders", which the king must tame. They are normally shown conquered or restrained, as in the Narmer Palette, or attacking other animals. But in Mesopotamian art they are shown in pairs, with intertwined necks.

claims.statement: World History Encyclopedia describes the largest engraving on the Narmer Palette as two men entwining the serpentine necks of unknown beasts.
claims.statement_id: World History Encyclopedia menggambarkan ukiran terbesar pada Palet Narmer sebagai dua pria yang melilitkan leher menyerupai ular milik hewan-hewan yang tidak dikenal.
claims.quote: Beneath this scene is the largest engraving on the palette of two men entwining the serpentine necks of unknown beasts.

claims.statement: These creatures have been interpreted as representing Upper and Lower Egypt, but nothing in this section justifies that interpretation, and no one has conclusively interpreted what it means.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk-makhluk itu pernah ditafsirkan sebagai lambang Mesir Hulu dan Mesir Hilir, tetapi tidak ada yang membenarkan tafsiran itu pada bagian tersebut, dan belum ada yang menafsirkan maknanya secara meyakinkan.
claims.quote: two men entwining the serpentine necks of unknown beasts. These creatures have been interpreted as representing Upper and Lower Egypt but there is nothing in this section to justify that interpretation. No one has conclusively interpreted what this section means.

claims.statement: There is no known name for the creature in any ancient texts.
claims.statement_id: Tidak ada nama yang diketahui bagi makhluk ini dalam teks kuno mana pun.
claims.quote: There is no known name for the creature in any ancient texts.

claims.statement: The image appears specifically on decorated cosmetic palettes from Egypt's Predynastic period, and more extensively as a design motif on cylinder seals of the Protoliterate period in Mesopotamia (circa 3500–3000 BC).
claims.statement_id: Gambar ini khususnya muncul pada palet kosmetik berhias dari periode Pradinasti Mesir, dan lebih luas sebagai motif desain pada segel silinder dari periode Protoliterat Mesopotamia (sekitar 3500–3000 SM).
claims.quote: The serpopard (also known as monstrous lion) is a mythical animal known from ancient Egyptian and Mesopotamian art. ... The image is featured specifically on decorated cosmetic palettes from the Predynastic period of Egypt, and more extensively, as design motifs on cylinder seals in the Protoliterate period of Mesopotamia (circa 3500–3000 BC).

claims.statement: Because birth tusks are associated with protecting mother and child during birth or birth ceremonies, serpopards are thought to play a role in this protection.
claims.statement_id: Karena gading kelahiran dikaitkan dengan perlindungan ibu dan anak saat persalinan atau upacara kelahiran, serpopard diperkirakan berperan dalam perlindungan itu.
claims.quote: Due to birth tusks being associated with the protection of mother and child during birth or birth ceremonies, serpopards are thought to play a role in this protection.

claims.statement: Wadj-wer is an Egyptian fertility deity connected with the Mediterranean and the Nile Delta’s waters.
claims.statement_id: Wadj-wer adalah dewa kesuburan Mesir yang terkait Laut Tengah dan kekayaan air Delta Nil.
claims.quote: Wadj-wer, also spelled Uatch-ur is an Egyptian god of fertility and the personification of the Mediterranean Sea, whose name means the "great green". He also symbolizes the richness of the waters of the Nile Delta.

claims.statement: Another interpretation links him with Nile Delta lagoons and lakes rather than only the Mediterranean.
claims.statement_id: Penafsiran lain menghubungkannya dengan laguna dan danau Delta Nil, bukan Laut Tengah saja.
claims.quote: It was commonly believed that Wadj-wer was a personification of the Mediterranean Sea; however, he also rather represented the lagoons and lakes in the northernmost Nile Delta, as suggested by some texts describing the "great green" as dry lands which could be crossed by foot, possibly a mention of pathways between two or more lakes.

claims.statement: He is attested in Sahure’s mortuary temple at Abusir in the Fifth Dynasty.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikenal dari kuil makam Sahure di Abusir pada Dinasti Kelima.
claims.quote: The earliest known attestation of Wadj-wer is dated back to the 5th Dynasty, in the mortuary temple of the pyramid of Sahure, at Abusir; here he appears similar to the god Hapi, but with his body filled by water ripples.

claims.statement: World History Encyclopedia describes Wadj-Wer (Uat-Ur) as the personification of the Mediterranean Sea whose name means "The Great Green".
claims.statement_id: World History Encyclopedia menyebut Wadj-Wer (Uat-Ur) sebagai personifikasi Laut Tengah yang namanya berarti "Yang Hijau Agung".
claims.quote: Wadj-Wer (Uat-Ur) - The personification of the Mediterranean Sea whose name means "The Great Green".

claims.statement: Recent scholarship has changed the traditional view of this god; he is now believed to have personified the lakes, swamps and lagoons of the Delta region near the Mediterranean.
claims.statement_id: Kajian terbaru mengubah pandangan tradisional tentang dewa ini; kini ia diyakini mempersonifikasikan danau, rawa, dan laguna di kawasan Delta dekat Laut Tengah.
claims.quote: Wadj-Wer (Uat-Ur) - The personification of the Mediterranean Sea whose name means "The Great Green". Recent scholarship has changed the traditional view of this god and he is now believed to have personified the lakes, swamps, and lagoons of the Delta region near to the Mediterranean.

claims.statement: Wilkinson notes inscriptions that refer to "crossing the great green" on foot, which would indicate a land crossing through the Delta region rather than the sea.
claims.statement_id: Wilkinson mencatat prasasti yang menyebut "menyeberangi yang hijau agung" dengan berjalan kaki, yang menunjukkan penyeberangan darat melalui kawasan Delta, bukan laut.
claims.quote: Wilkinson notes inscriptions which reference "crossing the great green" by foot which would indicate a land-crossing through the Delta region instead of the sea.

claims.statement: He was worshipped as early as the Old Kingdom (c. 2613-2181 BCE) and continued to be referenced through the rest of Egypt's history, especially on protective amulets and in tomb inscriptions.
claims.statement_id: Ia dipuja sejak Kerajaan Lama (sekitar 2613-2181 SM) dan terus disebut sepanjang sisa sejarah Mesir, terutama pada jimat pelindung dan prasasti makam.
claims.quote: Wadj-Wer (Uat-Ur) - The personification of the Mediterranean Sea ... He was worshipped as early as the Old Kingdom (c. 2613-2181 BCE) and continues to be referenced through the rest of Egypt's history, especially through protective amulets and tomb inscriptions.

claims.statement: Buchis is a sacred bull embodying the war god Montu’s ka.
claims.statement_id: Buchis adalah banteng suci sebagai perwujudan ka dewa perang Montu.
claims.quote: was the deification of the kꜣ ("power, life-force", Egyptological pronunciation ka) of the war god Montu as a sacred bull

claims.statement: The chosen bull must be white-bodied with a black face.
claims.statement_id: Banteng terpilih harus berwarna putih dengan wajah hitam.
claims.quote: a bull was required to have a white body and black face.

claims.statement: The bulls and their mothers are mummified and placed in the Bucheum cemetery.
claims.statement_id: Banteng dan ibunya dimumi serta ditempatkan di pemakaman Bucheum.
claims.quote: When these bulls – and in later times also their mothers – died, they were mummified, and placed in a special cemetery known as the Bucheum.

claims.statement: The cult begins toward the end of the pharaonic period, with an early burial known under Nectanebo II.
claims.statement_id: Kultusnya mulai menjelang akhir masa firaun; makam awal dikenal dari Nectanebo II.
claims.quote: Unlike the other Egyptian sacred bulls – the Apis and the Mnevis – the Buchis cult started towards the end of the pharaonic period, with the earliest known burial taking place in regnal year 14 of Nectanebo II (mid 4th century BC).

claims.statement: The last stela cited by the article records a bull’s death in 340 CE.
claims.statement_id: Stela terakhir yang disebut artikel mencatat kematian banteng pada tahun 340 M.
claims.quote: It is uncertain when the Buchis cult disappeared. The last confirmed tomb at the Bucheum is dated to the regnal year 12 of Diocletian (circa 295 CE), while the latest attestation of a Buchis burial is a stela reporting its installation in regnal year 33 of Diocletian (317 AD) and its demise in regnal year 57 of the same pharaoh (more precisely on 4 November 340 AD).

claims.statement: The accompanying source depicts Buchis as a running bull.
claims.statement_id: Sumber pendamping menggambarkan Buchis sebagai banteng berlari.
claims.quote: Buchis - Aspect of the Ka (life force/astral self) of the god Montu in the form of a live bull. Depicted as a bull running.

claims.statement: Nemty is an Egyptian god with a cult centre at Antaeopolis in Upper Egypt.
claims.statement_id: Nemty adalah dewa Mesir dengan pusat pemujaan di Antaeopolis, Mesir Hulu.
claims.quote: In Egyptian mythology, Nemty (Antaeus in Greek, but probably not connected to the Antaeus in Greek mythology) was a god whose worship centered at Antaeopolis in the northern part of Upper Egypt.

claims.statement: He has cult priests by at least the Second Dynasty.
claims.statement_id: Ia sudah memiliki pendeta kultus setidaknya pada Dinasti Kedua.
claims.quote: Nemty's worship is quite ancient, dating from at least the 2nd dynasty, at which point he already had priests dedicated to his cult. Originally, Nemty appears to have been the patron of the ancient area around Badari, which was the center of the cult of Horus.

claims.statement: Over time Nemty became considered the god of ferrymen and was depicted as a falcon standing on a boat, a reference to Horus; his later cult centre was in Antaeopolis and also in Per-Nemty (House of Nemty) in the 12th Upper Egyptian nome.
claims.statement_id: Lama-kelamaan Nemty dianggap sebagai dewa para tukang perahu dan digambarkan sebagai elang yang berdiri di atas perahu, rujukan pada Horus; pusat pemujaannya kemudian ada di Antaeopolis dan juga di Per-Nemty (Rumah Nemty) di nome Mesir Hulu ke-12.
claims.quote: Over time, Nemty became considered simply as the god of ferrymen and was consequently depicted as a falcon standing on a boat, a reference to Horus, who was originally considered as a falcon. As god of ferrymen, he gained the title Nemty, meaning "(one who) travels". His later cult center was in Antaeopolis, but also in Per-Nemty (House of Nemty) in the 12th Upper Egyptian nome.

claims.statement: In the tale The Contendings of Horus and Seth, Isis disguises herself as an old woman and Nemty unknowingly takes her across after being paid a gold ring.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah The Contendings of Horus and Seth, Isis menyamar sebagai perempuan tua dan Nemty tanpa sadar menyeberangkannya setelah dibayar sebuah cincin emas.
claims.quote: Nemty appears in the tale The Contendings of Horus and Seth which describes the settlement of the inheritance of Osiris ... Isis disguises herself as an old woman and unknowingly Nemty takes her across after being paid a gold ring

claims.statement: Two Sixth-Dynasty pharaohs have names incorporating Nemty.
claims.statement_id: Nama dua firaun Dinasti Keenam mengandung nama Nemty.
claims.quote: Two pharaohs bore theophoric names incorporating Nemty's, both during the Sixth Dynasty of Egypt at the end of the Old Kingdom period, Merenre Nemtyemsaf I and Merenre Nemtyemsaf II. Here Nemtyemsaf means "Nemty is his protection".

claims.statement: Older readings Anti or Anty are judged incorrect by several studies.
claims.statement_id: Pembacaan lama Anti atau Anty dinyatakan keliru oleh sejumlah studi.
claims.quote: In older literature, the hieroglyphs of the god were read as Anti or Anty. Several studies confirmed that this reading is not correct.

claims.statement: Nemti (formerly read Anti) is an ancient Egyptian deity securely attested from the Second Dynasty but possibly much older.
claims.statement_id: Nemti (dulu dibaca Anti) adalah dewa Mesir kuno yang terbukti pasti sejak Dinasti Kedua, tetapi mungkin jauh lebih tua.
claims.quote: Nemti (zu dt. „Der Reisende“), früher noch Anti gelesen, ist eine altägyptische Gottheit, die seit der 2. Dynastie sicher belegt ist, aber viel älter sein könnte.

claims.statement: He was regarded as the ferryman of the afterlife who carried the souls of the dead across the river of the underworld.
claims.statement_id: Ia dianggap sebagai tukang perahu alam baka yang mengangkut jiwa orang yang meninggal menyeberangi sungai alam baka.
claims.quote: Nemti (zu dt. „Der Reisende“), früher noch Anti gelesen, ist eine altägyptische Gottheit, die seit der 2. Dynastie sicher belegt ist, aber viel älter sein könnte. Er galt als Fährmann des Jenseits und transportierte die Seelen der Verstorbenen über den Jenseitsfluss.

claims.statement: He already appears on ceremonial palettes and mace heads of the Naqada II and Naqada III periods.
claims.statement_id: Ia sudah muncul pada palet upacara dan kepala gada dari zaman Naqada II dan Naqada III.
claims.quote: Nemti hat eine erstaunlich lange Kultgeschichte. Er erscheint bereits auf Prunkpaletten und Keulenknaufen der Naqada II und Naqada-III-Epoche.

claims.statement: Because little information survives, Nemty's original function is not well known, nor whether he was more than just a title of Horus referring to some specific function.
claims.statement_id: Karena informasi yang bertahan sedikit, fungsi asli Nemty tidak banyak diketahui, begitu pula apakah ia lebih dari sekadar gelar Horus untuk fungsi tertentu.
claims.quote: Due to lack of surviving information, it is not very well known what the original function of Nemty was or whether he was more than just a title of Horus referring to some specific function.

claims.statement: Seth fears magical intervention by Isis and so holds the gathering on an island, instructing Nemty not to allow anyone resembling Isis to be ferried there.
claims.statement_id: Seth takut akan campur tangan sihir Isis, sehingga ia mengadakan pertemuan di sebuah pulau dan menyuruh Nemty tidak menyeberangkan siapa pun yang mirip Isis ke sana.
claims.quote: Seth fears magical intervention by Isis, Horus' wife (in early Egyptian mythology), and so holds the gathering on an island, instructing Nemty not to allow anyone resembling Isis to be ferried there.

claims.statement: Imsety has a human head and guards the liver of the deceased, while the goddess Isis protects him.
claims.statement_id: Imsety berkepala manusia dan menjaga hati orang yang meninggal, sedangkan dewi Isis melindunginya.
claims.quote: イムセティは、人間の頭を持ち、死者の肝臓を守り、一方で女神イシスに守護される。ホルスからは、「持ち上げろ」と命じられており、死者を復活させるのを助ける役目を担っていたと見られる。

claims.statement: Isis protects Imsety.
claims.statement_id: Isis melindungi Imsety.
claims.quote: イムセティは、人間の頭を持ち、死者の肝臓を守り、一方で女神イシスに守護される。

claims.statement: In chapter 148 of the Book of the Dead the four sons of Horus are matched with the four directions, and Imsety corresponds to the south.
claims.statement_id: Dalam pasal 148 Kitab Orang Mati, keempat putra Horus dihubungkan dengan empat arah mata angin, dan Imsety sesuai dengan selatan.
claims.quote: 死者の書の第148章でホルスの4人の息子と4方位が対応付けされている。イムセティは南に対応する。 ドゥアムトエフ

claims.statement: World History Encyclopedia describes Imsety as a protector god, one of the Four Sons of Horus who protected the canopic jar holding the liver; he presided over the south, had the form of a human male, and was watched over by Isis.
claims.statement_id: World History Encyclopedia menyebut Imsety sebagai dewa pelindung, salah satu dari Empat Putra Horus yang melindungi bejana kanopi berisi hati; ia menguasai arah selatan, berwujud laki-laki manusia, dan diawasi oleh Isis.
claims.quote: Imsety - A protector god, one of the Four Sons of Horus who protected the canopic jar holding the liver. He presided over the south, had the form of a human male, and was watched over by Isis.

claims.statement: Most commonly, Imsety protected the liver, Hapy the lungs, Duamutef the stomach and Qebehsenuef the intestines, but this pattern often varied.
claims.statement_id: Paling umum, Imsety melindungi hati, Hapy paru-paru, Duamutef lambung, dan Qebehsenuef usus, tetapi pola ini sering berbeda-beda.
claims.quote: Most commonly, Imsety protected the liver, Hapy the lungs, Duamutef the stomach, and Qebehsenuef the intestines, but this pattern often varied.

claims.statement: In the latter part of the New Kingdom the four sons took on their most distinctive iconography: Imsety is portrayed as a human, Hapy as a baboon, Duamutef as a jackal and Qebehsenuef as a falcon; they had originally been portrayed as humans.
claims.statement_id: Pada akhir Kerajaan Baru keempat putra Horus mengambil ikonografi khas mereka: Imsety digambarkan sebagai manusia, Hapy sebagai babun, Duamutef sebagai jakal, dan Qebehsenuef sebagai elang; sebelumnya mereka digambarkan sebagai manusia.
claims.quote: The four sons of Horus were a group of four deities in ancient Egyptian religion ... Although they were originally portrayed as humans, in the latter part of the New Kingdom (c. 1550–1070 BC), they took on their most distinctive iconography, in which Imsety is portrayed as a human, Hapy as a baboon, Duamutef as a jackal, and Qebehsenuef as a falcon.

claims.statement: The Egyptologist James P. Allen translates Imsety's name as "He of the Dill"; another Egyptologist, Joshua Roberson, believes Imsety originated as a personification of this herb.
claims.statement_id: Egiptolog James P. Allen menerjemahkan nama Imsety sebagai "Ia dari Dill"; Egiptolog lain, Joshua Roberson, berpendapat Imsety bermula sebagai personifikasi herba dill itu.
claims.quote: The Egyptologist James P. Allen translates Hapy's name as "He of Haste" and Imsety as "He of the Dill"; another Egyptologist, Joshua Roberson, believes Imsety originated as a personification of this herb.

claims.statement: Imsety (jmstj, also Amset) is first mentioned in the Pyramid Texts, the earliest ancient Egyptian funerary texts, in the late Old Kingdom (24th and 23rd centuries BC).
claims.statement_id: Imsety (jmstj, juga Amset) pertama kali disebut dalam Teks Piramida, teks pemakaman Mesir kuno tertua, pada akhir Kerajaan Lama (abad ke-24 dan ke-23 SM).
claims.quote: Imsety (jmstj, also Amset), Hapy (ḥpy), Duamutef (dwꜣ-mwt.f), and Qebehsenuef (qbḥ-snw.f) are first mentioned in the Pyramid Texts, the earliest ancient Egyptian funerary texts, in the late Old Kingdom (24th and 23rd centuries BC).

claims.statement: Imsety's name also resembled the Egyptian word for "liver" (mjst), which may be the reason he became specifically linked with the liver.
claims.statement_id: Nama Imsety juga mirip dengan kata Mesir untuk "hati" (mjst), yang mungkin menjadi alasan ia dikaitkan secara khusus dengan hati.
claims.quote: Imsety's name also resembled the Egyptian word for "liver" (mjst), which may be the reason why he became specifically linked with the liver.

claims.statement: In numerous sources, such as Spell 541 of the Pyramid Texts, the four sons are stated to be the children of Horus, one of the major deities of the Egyptian pantheon.
claims.statement_id: Dalam banyak sumber, misalnya Mantra 541 Teks Piramida, keempat putra itu dinyatakan sebagai anak Horus, salah satu dewa utama panteon Mesir.
claims.quote: Imsety (jmstj, also Amset), Hapy (ḥpy), Duamutef (dwꜣ-mwt.f), and Qebehsenuef (qbḥ-snw.f) are first mentioned in the Pyramid Texts, the earliest ancient Egyptian funerary texts, in the late Old Kingdom (24th and 23rd centuries BC). In numerous sources, such as Spell 541 of the Pyramid Texts, they are stated to be the children of Horus, one of the major deities of the Egyptian pantheon.

claims.statement: Hatmehit is an Egyptian fish goddess attested from at least the Fourth Dynasty.
claims.statement_id: Hatmehit adalah dewi ikan Mesir yang diketahui setidaknya dari Dinasti Keempat.
claims.quote: Hatmehit, auch Hat-mehit, ist eine altägyptische Göttin, die bereits seit der 4. Dynastie als Fischgottheit belegt und eine Gaugöttin des 16. unterägyptischen Fischgaues ist. Sie wird als Frau mit einem welsartigen Fisch auf dem Kopf dargestellt, den sie dann auch über einem Uräus-Diadem trägt. Auf Amuletten erscheint sie als Fisch.

claims.statement: She is depicted as a woman with a fish on her head, or as a fish on amulets.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai perempuan dengan ikan di kepala atau sebagai ikan pada jimat.

claims.quote: Hatmehit was part of the Mendesian triad which consisted of her, the god Banebdjedet, and Harpocrates (Horus the child). Her cult was localized mainly to Nome 16 of Lower Egypt around Mendes although there are depictions of her found widely around Egypt.

claims.quote: In later periods Hatmehit takes on the iconography of Isis and Hathor, with her fish standard or crown replaced by the horns and sun disk that both shared.

claims.quote: In ancient Egyptian art, the Set animal, or sha, is the affiliated animal of the god Set. Because Set was identified with the Greek monster Typhon, the animal is also commonly known as the Typhonian animal or Typhonic beast.

claims.statement: Its identification with a real animal is uncertain and it may be fully mythical.
claims.statement_id: Identifikasinya dengan hewan nyata tidak pasti dan mungkin sepenuhnya mitologis.
claims.quote: Unlike other totemic animals, the Set animal is not easily identifiable in the modern animal world. It may have been fully mythological, or based on a combination of characteristics from real animals. The Set animal is one of the most frequently demonstrated animal determinatives.

claims.statement: A hieroglyph also depicts Set as a seated god with this animal’s head.
claims.statement_id: Hieroglif juga menggambarkan Set sebagai dewa duduk berkepala hewan ini.
claims.quote: The Set animal (Gardiner E20, E21,) is one of the portrayals of the god Set. The other common hieroglyph used to represent Set is a seated god with the head of the Set animal.

claims.statement: Its hieroglyph is a determinative for words connected with suffering, violence and storms.
claims.statement_id: Hieroglifnya menjadi penentu kata yang berhubungan dengan penderitaan, kekerasan, dan badai.
claims.quote: The linguistic use of these hieroglyphs in the Egyptian language is as the determinative for words portraying "items with chaos", example words related to "suffering, violence, perturbation", and also for "violent storms" of the atmosphere, a "tempest".

claims.statement: Its distinctive features are a stiff tail, angular upright ears and long muzzle.
claims.statement_id: Ciri khasnya berupa ekor kaku, telinga tegak bersudut, dan moncong panjang.
claims.quote: The sha is usually depicted as a slender canid, resembling a greyhound, fennec fox, or a jackal, with three distinguishing features: a stiff tail, often forked at the end, which stands straight up or at an angle, whether the animal is sitting, standing, or walking; its ears, also held erect, are usually depicted as squarish or triangular, narrowest at the base and widest at the squarish

claims.statement: World History Encyclopedia says Set is sometimes depicted as a shaggy red dog-like beast known as a sha (or, to modern-day scholars, the Set Animal).

claims.quote: Set, also known as Seth and Suetekh, was the Egyptian god of war, chaos, and storms ... He is sometimes depicted as a red-haired beast with a forked tail and cloven hooves or a shaggy red dog-like beast known as a sha (or, to modern-day scholars, as the Set Animal)

claims.quote: a shaggy red dog-like beast known as a sha (or, to modern-day scholars, as the Set Animal) which some scholars claim was modeled on the Saluki breed while others maintain was a purely mythological creature imagined specifically to represent Set

claims.quote: Drawings of the sha appear in Egyptian artwork from Naqada III until at least the period of the New Kingdom, a period of some two thousand years.

claims.quote: According to Egyptologist Richard H. Wilkinson, the first known use of the Set animal was upon the Scorpion Macehead of Scorpion II of Naqada III.

claims.quote: Was-sceptres represent the Set animal or Khnum. Was-sceptres were carried by gods, pharaohs and priests as a symbol of power and, in later use, control over the force of chaos (Set).

claims.statement: Egyptologist Ken Moss suggested that the Set animal is in fact the Saluki, an ancient breed of sighthound.

claims.quote: Egyptologist Ken Moss suggested the Set animal is in fact the Saluki, an ancient breed of sighthound.

claims.quote: The sha has no independent mythology associated with it that could aid with identification in either reality or fantasy, outside of its association with Set.

claims.statement: Medjed is a sacred ancient Egyptian fish of the elephantfish family, worshipped mainly in Oxyrhynchus (Per-Medjed), whose Egyptian name means "House of Medjed".

claims.statement: A settlement in Upper Egypt, Per-Medjed, was named after them. They are now better known by their Greek name Oxyrhynchus, meaning "sharp-nosed", a nod to the Egyptian depiction of the fish.

claims.quote: Medjed were a kind of elephantfish worshipped at Oxyrhynchus ... A settlement in Upper Egypt, Per-Medjed, was named after them. They are now better known by their Greek name Oxyrhynchus, meaning "sharp-nosed", a nod to the Egyptian depiction of the fish.

claims.quote: Medjed were a kind of elephantfish worshipped at Oxyrhynchus ... As a sacred fish, they are frequently depicted wearing horned sun-discs. Some figurines have rings to enable their wear as pendant amulets.

claims.statement: The fish were believed to have eaten the penis of the god Osiris after his brother Set had dismembered and scattered his body.

claims.statement_id: El Naddaha adalah roh perempuan dalam legenda Mesir yang memanggil laki-laki ke Nil hingga mati atau menghilang.
claims.quote: En-Naddāha (Egyptian Arabic: النداهة "the caller") is an Egyptian legend of a naiad-like female spirit who calls men to the Nile, leading to their death or disappearance. It is especially well known in the rural and agriculture-based areas of Egypt along the Nile and the Nile's water canals.

claims.statement: The legend’s origin is uncertain and it is more popular in rural settings.
claims.statement_id: Asal legenda ini tidak pasti dan lebih populer dalam lingkungan pedesaan.
claims.quote: The exact origin of this legend is unknown. The story was more popular during the 20th century when Egypt was less urban than it is now, and people would spend more time close to the Nile and the Nile's water canals. Children would play by its shores after school, and young men would chat there at night.

claims.statement: She calls men by name and makes them follow her voice in a hypnotized state.
claims.statement_id: Ia memanggil laki-laki dengan nama mereka dan membuat mereka mengikuti suaranya dalam keadaan terhipnosis.
claims.quote: En-Naddaha takes the form of stunningly beautiful woman who appears, as if by chance, to men walking by the Nile or the Nile's water canals at night. The men are usually a pair. The creature calls one by his first name, rendering him speechless, hypnotized, and obedient to her voice which he blindly follows, while the other man is unaffected, and attempts to pull the other back.

claims.statement: She is depicted as a beautiful young woman with long hair and loose clothing.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai perempuan muda cantik dengan rambut panjang dan busana longgar.
claims.quote: Usually the men do not get close enough to the Nile to get a glimpse of what the creature looks like before they run away. In rare instances, they get a glimpse of her. She is described as being a very beautiful young woman; tall, slender, with long flowing hair down her back.

claims.statement: Some tales delay the victim’s departure for several nights after the call.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian kisah menunda keberangkatan korban sampai beberapa malam setelah panggilan.
claims.quote: In rural Egypt, where the legend is prominent, the creature may call for men in their homes by the shores of the Nile and the Nile's water canals, who then eagerly attempt to leave home for her. Ils sont représentés par un groupe de trois ou quatre chacals noirs qui tirent la barque solaire de Rê lors de son voyage nocturne. Ils sont aussi amenés à le protéger contre le mal.

claims.statement: They protect Ra from evil.
claims.statement_id: Mereka melindungi Ra dari kejahatan.
claims.quote: Ils sont aussi amenés à le protéger contre le mal. Ils sont également parfois représentés comme des oiseaux à têtes de chacals

claims.statement: The name Baou Imenty means spirits of the west.
claims.statement_id: Nama Baou Imenty berarti roh-roh barat.
claims.quote: Baou Imenty (Bȝw Imnty) est le nom égyptien des esprits de l'Ouest. Il signifie « esprits de l'Occident ».

claims.statement: Their images are known from Ramesside times and occur in afterlife texts.
claims.statement_id: Gambar mereka dikenal dari masa Ramesside dan muncul dalam teks akhirat.
claims.quote: Ils sont apparus pour la première fois au cours de la période ramesside au Nouvel Empire. Mais il y a quelques mentions d'eux, un peu avant, dans les textes des sarcophages et le Livre des Morts. Ils figurent dans de nombreux textes sur l'au-delà et il n'est pas rare de les voir sur des situles en bronze, sortes de seaux cérémoniels en forme de poitrine.

claims.statement: The Greif is a hybrid creature in Egyptian mythology appearing on predynastic palettes.
claims.statement_id: Greif adalah makhluk campuran dalam mitologi Mesir yang muncul sejak palet masa pradinasti.
claims.quote: „Greif“ (altägyptisch Sefer, Sefre, Seferer, Sefrer; auch Achech, Teschtesch; demotisch Sereref, Serref) ist die Bezeichnung eines Fabelwesens in der altägyptischen Mythologie, das unter anderem bereits auf der Zwei-Hunde-Palette der prädynastischen Epoche fester Bestandteil des Bildprogrammes war.

claims.statement: Its form develops from predatory-bird features into forms with pantherlike hide and a falcon head.
claims.statement_id: Bentuknya berkembang dari ciri burung pemangsa menjadi wujud dengan kulit mirip panter dan kepala elang.
claims.quote: Der frühdynastische Greif hatte raubtierartige Züge eines Geiers, der kammähnliche Flügel auf der Mitte des Rückens besaß. Im Mittleren Reich entwickelte sich eine ähnliche Form mit flachem Kopf; zusätzlich mit pantherähnlichem Fell, Menschenkopf zwischen den Flügeln und Halsband. Sein Wesen war unter anderem darauf ausgerichtet, Dämonen und unheilvolle Handlungen abzuwenden.

claims.statement: In the Eighteenth Dynasty its depiction receives influences from outside Egypt.
claims.statement_id: Pada Dinasti Kedelapan Belas penggambarannya menerima pengaruh luar Mesir.
claims.quote: In der 18. Dynastie fand ein neuer ikonografischer Typus des Greifs mit außerägyptischen Einflüssen Eingang in die altägyptische Mythologie. Der Kopf, der wieder einem Geier ähnelte, wies in Kombination mit pferdeähnlichen Beinen schlankere Proportionen auf, die möglicherweise aus dem syrischen Raum stammten.

claims.statement: One fable gives it a falcon’s beak, human eyes, lion limbs, fish ears and a snake tail.
claims.statement_id: Satu dongeng memberi paruh elang, mata manusia, anggota singa, telinga ikan, dan ekor ular.
claims.quote: „Sein Schnabel ist der eines Falken, seine Augen die eines Menschen, seine Glieder die eines Löwen, seine Ohren die eines Fisches, sein Schwanz der einer Schlange.“

claims.statement: It can function as a protective solar eye or a desert hunting creature.
claims.statement_id: Ia dapat berfungsi sebagai matahari pelindung atau makhluk pemburu gurun.
claims.quote: Der Greif ist bereits sehr früh als mythologisches Jagdtier belegt, das in der Wüste tätig war. Alternativ fungierte der Greif in seiner Erscheinungsform als schützendes Sonnenauge, das vom Sonnengott Re als Vergeltung eingesetzt wurde:

claims.statement: The Malay Dewa Nun article identifies its figure as a god of chaos and primordial time.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Melayu Dewa Nun mengenali tokohnya sebagai dewa kekacauan dan masa primordial.
claims.quote: Dewa Nun merupakan dewa kacau bilau dan zaman awal ("primordial.")

claims.statement: Nun in the accompanying source is primordial water before the world emerges.
claims.statement_id: Nun dalam sumber pendamping merupakan air primordial sebelum dunia muncul.
claims.quote: Nu (Nun) and Naunet - Nu was the personification of the primordial chaos from which the world arose. Naunet is his female aspect and consort. Nu is commonly regarded as "Father of the Gods" while Naunet is only referenced regarding the Ogdoad, the grouping of eight primordial gods, four males matching four females, who represent the original elements of creation.

claims.statement: Nun's consort (or his female aspect) was the goddess Nunut or Naunet.
claims.statement_id: Pasangan Nun (atau aspek perempuannya) adalah dewi Nunut atau Naunet.
claims.quote: Nun's consort (or his female aspect) was the goddess Nunut or Naunet

claims.statement: World History Encyclopedia calls Naunet the female aspect and consort of Nu, referenced only in connection with the Ogdoad, the grouping of eight primordial gods.
claims.statement_id: World History Encyclopedia menyebut Naunet sebagai aspek perempuan sekaligus pasangan Nu, dan hanya disebut dalam kaitannya dengan Ogdoad, kelompok delapan dewa purba.
claims.quote: Nu (Nun) and Naunet - Nu was the personification of the primordial chaos from which the world arose. Naunet is his female aspect and consort. Nu is commonly regarded as "Father of the Gods" while Naunet is only referenced regarding the Ogdoad, the grouping of eight primordial gods, four males matching four females, who represent the original elements of creation.

claims.statement: Naunet (also spelt Nunet) is the female aspect, which is the name Nu with a female gender ending; the male aspect, Nun, is written with a male gender ending.
claims.statement_id: Naunet (juga ditulis Nunet) adalah aspek perempuan, yaitu nama Nu dengan akhiran gramatikal perempuan; aspek laki-lakinya, Nun, ditulis dengan akhiran laki-laki.
claims.quote: Naunet (also spelt Nunet) is the female aspect, which is the name Nu with a female gender ending. The male aspect, Nun, is written with a male gender ending.

claims.statement: According to World History Encyclopedia, the Ogdoad is the eight gods representing primordial elements of creation: Nu and Naunet (water), Heh and Hauhet (infinity), Kek and Kauket (darkness), and Amun and Amaunet (hiddenness, obscurity).
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Ogdoad adalah delapan dewa yang mewakili unsur purba penciptaan: Nu dan Naunet (air), Heh dan Hauhet (ketakterhinggaan), Kek dan Kauket (kegelapan), serta Amun dan Amaunet (ketersembunyian).
claims.quote: Ogdoad - The eight gods representing primordial elements of creation: Nu and Naunet (water); Heh and Hauhet (infinity); Kek and Kauket (darkness); Amun and Amaunet (hiddenness, obscurity).

claims.statement: The Ogdoad includes Naunet and Nun, Amaunet and Amun, Hauhet and Heh, and Kauket and Kek.
claims.statement_id: Ogdoad mencakup Naunet dan Nun, Amaunet dan Amun, Hauhet dan Heh, serta Kauket dan Kek.
claims.quote: The Ogdoad includes along with Naunet and Nun, Amaunet and Amun; Hauhet and Heh; and Kauket and Kek.

claims.statement: According to Encyclopedia.com, the Ogdoad is a group of deities that includes Nu(n) and Naunet (representing the primeval water and formlessness), Huh and Huhet, Kek and Keket, and Amun and Amaunet.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Encyclopedia.com, Ogdoad adalah kelompok dewa yang mencakup Nu(n) dan Naunet (mewakili air purba dan ketakberbentukan), Huh dan Huhet, Kek dan Keket, serta Amun dan Amaunet.
claims.quote: The gods of this cosmogony form an Ogdoad, or group of eight pairs of deities. This group includes Nu(n) and Naunet (representing the primeval water and formlessness), Huh and Huhet (spaciousness), Kek and Keket (darkness), and Amun and Amaunet (concealment).

claims.statement: According to World History Encyclopedia, Ptah was sometimes known as Ptah-Nun or Ptah-Naunet in his creative aspect, linking him with the primordial substances of the Ogdoad.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Ptah kadang dikenal sebagai Ptah-Nun atau Ptah-Naunet dalam aspek penciptanya, yang menghubungkannya dengan zat purba Ogdoad.
claims.quote: Ptah - One of the oldest Egyptian gods ... He was sometimes known as Ptah-Nun or Ptah-Naunet in his creative aspect, linking him with the primordial substances of the Ogdoad.

claims.statement: In ancient Egyptian religion, Nun, the male aspect paired with Naunet, is the personification of the primordial watery abyss that existed at the time of creation and from which the creator sun god Ra arose.
claims.statement_id: Dalam agama Mesir kuno, Nun, aspek laki-laki yang berpasangan dengan Naunet, adalah personifikasi jurang air purba yang ada pada saat penciptaan dan tempat dewa matahari pencipta Ra muncul.
claims.quote: Nun ("The Inert One") or Nu ("Watery One") ... in ancient Egyptian religion, is the personification of the primordial watery abyss which existed at the time of creation and from which the creator sun god Ra arose.

claims.statement: Abyzou is a female demon in Near Eastern and European traditions associated with miscarriage and infant death.
claims.statement_id: Abyzou adalah setan perempuan dalam tradisi Timur Dekat dan Eropa yang dikaitkan dengan keguguran dan kematian bayi.
claims.quote: In the folklore of the Near East and Europe, Abyzou is a female demon associated with miscarriages and infant mortality, motivated by envy over her own infertility. In Coptic Egypt, she is identified with Alabasandria, and in Byzantine culture with Gylou.

claims.statement: Coptic tradition links her with Alabasandria, while Byzantine tradition associates her with Gylou.
claims.statement_id: Nama Alabasandria dalam tradisi Koptik dan Gylou dalam tradisi Bizantium dihubungkan dengan Abyzou.
claims.quote: In Coptic Egypt, she is identified with Alabasandria, and in Byzantine culture with Gylou.

claims.statement: Her fuller literary depiction occurs in the Testament of Solomon.
claims.statement_id: Penggambaran sastra lengkapnya terdapat dalam Testament of Solomon.
claims.quote: Abyzou (also spelled Abizou, Obizu, Obizuth, Obyzouth, Byzou etc.) is pictured on amulets with fish- or serpent-like attributes. Her fullest literary depiction is from the compendium of demonology known as the Testament of Solomon, dated variously by scholars from as early as the 1st century CE to as late as the 4th.

claims.statement: Amulets depict her with fishlike or serpentine attributes.
claims.statement_id: Jimat menggambarkannya dengan unsur ikan atau ular.
claims.quote: is pictured on amulets with fish- or serpent-like attributes.

claims.statement: The Testament of Solomon tells of Solomon binding her hair and displaying her before the temple.
claims.statement_id: Testament of Solomon mengisahkan Solomon membelenggu rambutnya dan memajangnya di depan kuil.
claims.quote: Solomon orders that she be chained by her own hair and hung up in front of the Temple in public view.

claims.statement: Obizuth in the translated Testament of Solomon says she roams at night and attacks newborn children.
claims.statement_id: Obizuth dalam terjemahan Testament of Solomon berkata ia berkeliling pada malam hari dan menyerang anak yang baru lahir.
claims.quote: I am called among men Obizuth; and by night I sleep not, but go my rounds over all the world, and visit women in childbirth.

claims.statement: Caliadne is a Nile naiad in Greek mythology, possibly a daughter of the river god Nilus.
claims.statement_id: Caliadne adalah naiad Nil dalam mitologi Yunani, kemungkinan putri dewa sungai Nilus.
claims.quote: in Greek mythology, was a naiad of the river Nile, presumably one of the daughters of the river-god Nilus.

claims.statement: She was one of the wives of King Aegyptus of Egypt and bore him twelve sons.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjadi salah satu istri Raja Aegyptus dari Mesir dan melahirkan dua belas putra baginya.
claims.quote: She was one of the wives of King Aegyptus of Egypt, bearing him twelve sons

claims.statement: Her sons marry Polyxo and Danaus’s daughters and are killed on their wedding night.
claims.statement_id: Putra-putranya menikahi putri Polyxo dan Danaus, lalu dibunuh pada malam pernikahan.
claims.quote: These sons married and were murdered by the daughters of her sister Polyxo and King Danaus of Libya during their wedding night.

claims.statement: The Apollodorus quotation at Theoi names a Naiad nymph called Kaliadne (Caliadne) in connection with drawing lots for the daughters of Polyxo, also a Naiad.
claims.statement_id: Kutipan Apollodorus di Theoi menyebut seorang naiad bernama Kaliadne (Caliadne) dalam kaitannya dengan undian untuk putri-putri Polyxo, yang juga seorang naiad.
claims.quote: a Naias Nymphe (Naiad Nymph) named Kaliadne (Caliadne) drew lots for the daughters of [Danaus and] Polyxo, also a Naias (Naiad).

claims.statement: The sons were named Eurylochus, Phantes, Peristhenes, Hermus, Dryas, Potamon, Cisseus, Lixus, Imbros, Bromios, Polyctor and Chthonius.
claims.statement_id: Putra-putra itu bernama Eurylochus, Phantes, Peristhenes, Hermus, Dryas, Potamon, Cisseus, Lixus, Imbros, Bromios, Polyctor, dan Chthonius.
claims.quote: a Naias Nymphe (Naiad Nymph) named Kaliadne (Caliadne) drew lots for the daughters of [Danaus and] Polyxo, also a Naias (Naiad). The sons were named Eurylokhos (Eurylochus), Phantes, Peristhenes, Hermos (Hermus), Dryas, Potamon, Kisseus (Cisseus), Lixos (Lixus), Imbros, Bromios, Polyktor (Polyctor), and Khthonios (Chthonius)

claims.statement: According to Hippostratus, Aegyptus had his progeny by a single woman called Eurryroe, daughter of the river-god Nilus.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Hippostratus, Aegyptus memperoleh keturunannya dari satu perempuan saja bernama Eurryroe, putri dewa sungai Nilus.
claims.quote: According to Hippostratus, Aegyptus had his progeny by a single woman called Eurryroe, daughter of the river-god Nilus.

claims.statement: In Apollodorus (Frazer's translation at Theoi), the twelve sons of Egyptus by the Naiad nymph Caliadne cast lots for the daughters of Danaus by the Naiad nymph Polyxo.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Apollodorus (terjemahan Frazer di Theoi), kedua belas putra Egyptus dari naiad Caliadne mengundi putri-putri Danaus dari naiad Polyxo.
claims.quote: The twelve sons of Egyptus by the Naiad nymph Caliadne cast lots for the daughters of Danaus by the Naiad nymph Polyxo

claims.statement: In Apollodorus, Lynceus and Proteus had been borne to Egyptus by a woman of royal blood, Argyphia, so Egyptus had sons by several mothers.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Apollodorus, Lynceus dan Proteus dilahirkan bagi Egyptus oleh seorang perempuan berdarah bangsawan, Argyphia, sehingga Egyptus memiliki putra dari beberapa ibu.
claims.quote: for Lynceus and Proteus had been borne to Egyptus by a woman of royal blood, Argyphia
